blocks.text: DSPM scans Azure Cosmos DB accounts for sensitive data and misconfigurations.
You can use the Terraform template or an Azure CLI command available in the Zscaler Admin Console and apply it to the Cosmos DB accounts.
To perform data plane scanning, you must manually grant the necessary read permissions in your Azure environment to DSPM. DSPM does not configure data plane permissions automatically.
Before registering an Azure Cosmos DB account for scanning, ensure the following prerequisites are met:

blocks.item: The Microsoft Entra tenant hosting the Cosmos DB accounts is onboarded to DSPM.
Access to your Azure environment with all the required permissions.

blocks.heading: Adding an Azure Cosmos DB Account

blocks.text: The following flowchart illustrates the available paths for registering Azure Cosmos DB accounts based on whether you are configuring single or multiple database instances.
To add an Azure Cosmos DB account:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > Service Registration.
On the Service Registration page, select the Azure Cosmos DB tab.
A table displays all Azure Cosmos DB accounts discovered within your onboarded subscriptions.
See image.
Choose one of the following methods to register the accounts:
Register Accounts Using Terraform
Use a Terraform template for the DSPM integration and to apply permissions across multiple accounts at the same time.
On the Azure Cosmos DB tab, click + Get Registration Template.
The Get Cosmos DB Registration Template drawer appears.
In the Get Cosmos DB Registration Template drawer, select the appropriate Azure Integration from the drop-down menu.
The Scanner Role Managed Identity ID is displayed for the selected integration.
Click Copy Code Snippet to copy the Terraform code snippet to the clipboard.
Apply the code snippet in your Terraform environment for the Azure Cosmos DB accounts to grant the necessary permissions.
This script creates the necessary custom data plane reader role and assigns it to the DSPM scanner's managed identity role.
See image.
Register Account Using Azure CLI
Use a CLI command to configure permissions for an individual Azure Cosmos DB account.
On the Azure Cosmos DB tab, click the menu (⋮) for the required Cosmos DB account and select Get Registration Command.
The Get Cosmos DB Registration CLI Command drawer appears.
In the Get Cosmos DB Registration CLI Command drawer, click Copy Azure CLI Command Script to copy the Azure CLI script to the clipboard.
Run the command in your Azure CLI environment to assign the required permissions.
See image.

blocks.text: If permissions are not granted using one of the preceding methods, the scans fail and an error message is displayed in the scan logs indicating a permissions issue.

blocks.heading: Deleting a Registered Azure Cosmos DB Account

blocks.text: To remove DSPM's access to a registered Azure Cosmos DB account, you must manually delete the role assignment within your Azure environment. This action ensures that DSPM no longer has permissions to access the account.
No action is required in the Zscaler Admin Console to remove an Azure Cosmos DB account registration. Permissions are managed by the Azure tenant.
